transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is… I feel like I’m always moving from one thing to the next, like I can’t really just sit and idle, if that makes sense. And with the new setup at work, it’s gotten harder to sort of hide that.

I do customer service, so there’s always something going on anyway, calls and screens and all that, and I used to kind of blend in with the busy-ness. But now it’s like… I notice it more, or other people notice it more. I’ll be shifting from one thing to another before I’ve even settled into the first thing. It’s not like I’m trying to be difficult. It’s just how I seem to run.

Thinking back, can you tell me whether you noticed this kind of restlessness and jumping between tasks as far back as childhood or school years, or is this something that really only started in adulthood?

No, it was definitely around before this job. I mean, the job change made it more obvious, but thinking back, school was kind of the same story.

I remember in grade school, teachers would write things like I was bright but careless, or that I talked out of turn. And there was always that note about needing reminders to stay with my work. My mom kept some of those report cards for years, actually—she had this drawer with all kinds of school papers and old photos, and every now and then she’d pull them out. But yeah, the comments were pretty consistent. It wasn’t something that just started when I got older.

Besides jumping between tasks, do you also notice things like feeling physically restless, needing to move or fidget, or often interrupting others and acting impulsively before thinking things through?

Yeah, the restless part, for sure. Like if I have to sit through one of those training videos at work, especially the slow ones where they’re just reading off slides, I start feeling kind of boxed in. I’ll want to stand up, or stretch, or I’ll be messing with a pen or something in my hands.

Same thing at an appointment if it’s running slow. I’m sitting there trying to be polite, but inside I’m kind of like, okay, I need to move. It’s not dramatic, I don’t think, but it’s there.
Beyond work, do these patterns of restlessness and jumping between tasks also cause noticeable problems in your personal life—like with relationships, managing chores, or social situations?

Yeah, I mean… at home it’s there too, I guess, but the place it’s really starting to matter is work. Which is funny because I usually get along with customers pretty well—people will say I’m friendly, and I do try hard.

But lately it’s been showing up in my reviews. Supervisors have pointed out that I’ll leave tickets unfinished, or I’ll make these little mistakes that end up slowing the team down. And I hate that, because it’s not like I don’t care. I’ll be working on something, then something else grabs my attention, and then later I realize, oh, I never actually finished that first thing.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others in conversation, blurting out answers before someone finishes a question, or acting on impulse without thinking things through first?

Yeah… I do that sometimes. I don’t mean to be rude or take over, but if I hear coworkers working through a customer problem, I’ll kind of jump in with the answer before they’ve finished talking it through, or before anyone actually asked me.

It’s like I hear where it’s going and I’m already saying it. Then afterward I realize, okay, maybe I should’ve let them finish.
